367410.title: Turán bound for suspensions of arbitrary trees

{\rm ex}(n,\widehat{T})\le f(n,k).

367789.title: Helme-Guizon–Przytycki–Rong torsion conjecture for chromatic homology
367789.literal_statement:

368492.title: Generalised Common Neighbour Conjecture for Saxl hypergraphs
368492.literal_statement: Let $G\leq \operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a finite permutation group with base size $b(G)\geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{H}(G)$ be its Saxl hypergraph; in the original graph formulation, use $\Sigma(G)$. **Generalised Common Neighbour Conjecture.** For any distinct points $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega$, there exist a third point $\gamma\in\Omega\setminus\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and edges $E_\alpha,E_\beta$ of $\mathcal{H}(G)$ such that $\alpha,\gamma\in E_\alpha$ and $\beta,\gamma\in E_\beta$. This formulation generalises the common-neighbour property from Saxl graphs to Saxl hypergraphs; the supplied source gives no resolution.
368492.review_depth: literal_statement_and_primary_target_context; depth is detailed in attempts, not an all-paper audit
368492.mathematical_disposition_and_remaining_g: Public theorem gives, for every B>=2 and every degree bound, a finite faithful primitive group of base size B with two nonadjacent points having no common neighbour. Generalized Saxl edges are pairs contained in minimum bases, precisely the 2-section of the source Saxl hypergraph. This already refutes the reserved universal claim, including primitive scope.

368836.title: The clique-cutset conjecture for minimally non-perfectly divisible graphs
368836.literal_statement:
Let $G$) be a graph. A graph is **perfectly divisible** if every induced subgraph with at least one edge has a partition $(A,B)$ such that the induced graph on $A$ is perfect and $(G[B])<(G)$. A graph is **minimally non-perfectly divisible** (MNPD) if it is not perfectly divisible but every proper induced subgraph is perfectly divisible. A **clique cutset** is a clique whose deletion disconnects $G$.

**Clique-cutset conjecture.** No MNPD graph contains a clique cutset.

This conjecture is proposed as an analogue of the folklore result that no minimal imperfect graph contains a clique cutset. Its status is open.

368836.mathematical_disposition_and_remaining_g: Every atlas graph through order 7 and every tested random graph through order 13 was perfectly divisible; no MNPD clique-cutset violation found. The invalid published proof cannot be repaired merely by taking A1 union A2: clique-cutset vertices assigned differently can create an odd hole on one side. Need a compatible perfect maximum-clique transversal extension, or an independent MNPD witness.

368837.title: The P5-free perfect divisibility conjecture
368837.literal_statement:
Let $P_5$ denote the chordless path on five vertices. A graph is **perfectly divisible** if every induced subgraph with at least one edge has a partition $(A,B)$ such that the induced graph on $A$ is perfect and $(G[B])<(G)$.

**P5-free conjecture.** Every $P_5$-free graph is perfectly divisible.

The conjecture is proposed in connection with the paper's clique-cutset results. Chudnovsky and Sivaraman proved the related result that $(P_5,\operatorname{bull})$-free graphs are perfectly divisible; the stated conjecture remains open.
